the development and application of a high-speed rotary-spinning technique for preparation of polyvinyl-pyrrolidone micro- and nanoscale fibers with controlled micro- and macrostructure and their application as a drug delivery system.
the development of the rotary-spinning technique and the characterization of polymeric fibers for the application in drug delivery systems.
the application of high-speed rotational spinning for preparation of fibrous intermediates for conventional dosage forms and drug delivery systems.

the micro- and macrostructure of the fibers is strongly related to their mechanical properties and that the free volume changes can be used as an indicator of the microstructural changes.
the high-speed rotary spinning method is an effective and promising tool for the preparation of polymeric micro- and nanoscale fibers.
the micro- and macrostructure characterization of PVP and PVP-VA rotary-spun fibers is a useful tool for the preparation of dosage forms of desired properties.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the high-speed rotary spinning of poly(vinyl pyrrolidone) and poly(viny pyrrolid one-vinyl acetate) solutions enables preparation of fibrous matrices with a wide range of mechanical and morphological properties.
the PALS technique is a powerful and useful tool for studying microstructural changes of polymeric materials and for correlating them with mechanical properties.

the micro- and macroscopic characterization of fibers prepared from PVP and PVP VA by the rotary spinning technique is feasible and can provide a useful basis for further studies on the application of these materials in drug delivery systems and solid dosage forms.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the microstructural changes in PVP and PVP VA fibers are related to the mechanical properties and that the PALS method can be successfully used for the screening of fiber properties and for the development of novel dosage forms.
the microstructural characterization of polymeric fibers is a crucial factor for their application in the pharmaceutical industry.
